facts.fact_text: A demonstration was held on 11 March 2011.
A demonstration was held on 20 October 2012.
A demonstration was held on 17 November 2012.
The second applicant attended the demonstration of 11 March 2011.
The second applicant attended the demonstration of 20 October 2012.
The first applicant attended the demonstration of 20 October 2012.
The first applicant attended the demonstration of 17 November 2012.
According to the first applicant, he also intended to participate in the demonstration of 11 March 2011.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful and were conducted in a peaceful manner.
In the course of many of those unauthorised peaceful demonstrations, both applicants were arrested and convicted.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) refused to authorise the demonstration of 20 October 2012 at the site indicated by the organisers.

The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) proposed another location for the demonstration of 20 October 2012, namely the grounds of a driving school situated in the 20th habitable area of the Sabail District on the outskirts of Baku.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) refused to authorise the demonstration of 17 November 2012.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) noted in general terms that the assembly of 17 November 2012 would not be in accordance with the Law on Freedom of Assembly.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) noted that the square where the organisers proposed to hold the assembly of 17 November 2012 was a designated public leisure area.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) noted that the assembly of 17 November 2012 itself would be impractical.
All three demonstrations of 11 March 2011, 20 October 2012, and 17 November 2012 were dispersed as soon as the protesters began to gather.
Both applicants were arrested during the dispersal operations of the demonstrations of 11 March 2011, 20 October 2012, and 17 November 2012.
After each arrest during the demonstrations of 11 March 2011, 20 October 2012, and 17 November 2012, both applicants were taken to police station no. 9 of the Sabail district police office.

On the day of each of the applicants' respective arrests during the demonstrations of 11 March 2011, 20 October 2012, and 17 November 2012, administrative-offence reports were issued in respect of them.

In each case following the demonstrations of 11 March 2011, 20 October 2012, and 17 November 2012, the applicants were charged with an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer).
Following their arrest on 20 October 2012, the applicants were additionally charged under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences (violation of rules on holding public assemblies).
It appears that the organisers of the demonstration of 11 March 2011 gave no proper prior notice to the Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA).
Prior to the demonstration of 20 October 2012, on 15 October 2012 the organisers gave notice to the Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA).
Prior to the demonstration of 17 November 2012, on 12 November 2012 the organisers gave notice to the Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA).
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) refused to authorise the demonstration of 20 October 2012 at the site indicated by the organisers.

The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) proposed another location for the demonstration of 20 October 2012, namely the grounds of a driving school situated in the 20th habitable area of the Sabail District on the outskirts of Baku.

The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) noted that the square where the organisers proposed to hold the assembly of 17 November 2012 was a designated public leisure area.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) noted that the assembly of 17 November 2012 itself would be impractical.

According to the applicants, the respective hearings before the Sabail District Court were very brief.

According to the applicants, members of the public were not allowed inside the courtroom during the hearings before the Sabail District Court, even though the court had not taken a formal decision to close the hearings to the public.
According to the applicants, they were not given an opportunity to appoint lawyers of their own choosing at the hearings before the Sabail District Court.
A State-funded lawyer was appointed to defend each of the applicants at each hearing before the Sabail District Court.

According to the transcript of the Sabail District Court hearing of 11 March 2011, the State-funded lawyer for the second applicant (Mr V.M.) briefly asked the court in his oral submissions to consider the young age of the second applicant and his sincere regret for having committed the administrative offence.

None of the material submitted to the Court contains any record showing that at the hearing of 20 October 2012 the State-funded lawyer for the second applicant (Mr K.B.) made any oral or written submissions on behalf of the second applicant.

None of the material submitted to the Court contains any record showing that at the hearing of 17 November 2012 the State-funded lawyer for the first applicant (Mr Z.A.) made any oral or written submissions on behalf of the first applicant.

According to a statement (ərizə) signed by the first applicant, he refused the assistance of the State-funded lawyer at the Sabail District Court hearing of 20 October 2012 and decided to defend himself in person.
During the Sabail District Court hearing of 20 October 2012, the court did not question any witnesses.
During the Sabail District Court hearing of 17 November 2012, the court did not question any witnesses.
In each case the Sabail District Court found that the applicants had failed to stop participating in an unauthorised demonstration.

The Sabail District Court convicted the applicants under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer) in each case related to the demonstrations of 11 March 2011, 20 October 2012, and 17 November 2012.

In the proceedings related to his participation in the demonstration of 20 October 2012, the second applicant was also convicted by the Sabail District Court under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences (violation of rules on holding public assemblies).
The applicants were sentenced to various periods of administrative detention as set out in the Appendix.
According to the first applicant, he was never served with a copy of the administrative-offence report or with other documents from his case file following his arrest on 4 March 2011.
According to the first applicant, he was not given access to a lawyer after his arrest on 4 March 2011 or while he was in police custody.
According to the first applicant, until 6 March 2011 his whereabouts were unknown to his family and friends.
Only on 7 March 2011 was a lawyer hired by the first applicant's family able to meet the first applicant and to learn the details of his arrest, detention and the court proceedings against him.
The first applicant applied to the Baku Court of Appeal to have his mobile-phone call records examined in respect of the date and time of the alleged administrative offence on 4 March 2011.

The Baku Court of Appeal did not address the first applicant's request to have his mobile-phone call records examined in respect of the date and time of the alleged administrative offence on 4 March 2011.

According to the applicants, they were not given an opportunity to appoint lawyers of their own choosing at the hearings before the Sabail District Court.

According to a statement (ərizə) signed by the first applicant, he refused the assistance of the State-funded lawyer at the Sabail District Court hearing of 20 October 2012 and decided to defend himself in person.
The only witnesses questioned during the Sabail District Court hearing of 11 March 2011 concerning the second applicant were police officers who, according to official records, had arrested him.

At the Sabail District Court hearing of 11 March 2011, the police officers testified that together with some other people the second applicant had attempted to hold an unlawful demonstration and continued to protest despite the order to disperse.
During the Sabail District Court hearing of 20 October 2012, the court did not question any witnesses.
During the Sabail District Court hearing of 17 November 2012, the court did not question any witnesses.
